column1: # Snowflake token forms for generated compat rows: the text written for each
# value SnowflakeDocs.g4 names by class, where the docs write a <placeholder>.
# Keywords and punctuation are literals in the grammar and need no row.
# A sample of one name, string or number stands for its class when the docs
# judge reads a statement; a keyword or a sample of several tokens stands for
# itself. (reserved) marks a word the docs judge never reads as a name.

column3: unquoted identifier: a letter or _, then letters, digits, _ and $; a "double-quoted" one is a name too
(qualified) a schema object's name, as an ID, which db.schema.name may qualify
(qualified 2) a database's schema or database role, as an ID, which db.name may qualify
single-quoted string constant; a $$dollar-quoted$$ one is a string too
an expression; the command pages give no expression grammar, so a constant
a query; the command pages give no query grammar beyond SELECT's list
<copy_statement>: a COPY INTO <table> statement, as CREATE PIPE's body is
a data type; INT is a synonym of NUMBER(38,0)
(path) @<stage>: a named stage, its path after a slash, quoted when it has spaces; @~ is the user's stage and @%t a table's
$<col_position>: a column of a staged file by its position
$<session_variable>: a session variable by its name
file://<path>/<file>: a local file or directory in PUT and GET, an absolute path, written without quotes

column1: # Reserved keywords: those the page marks reserved by ANSI or by Snowflake.
# The ones it reserves only in a context (a SHOW's IN, a column in a scalar
# expression, a table in FROM) are not listed, since the docs judge has no
# Optional clauses tried at every site a page's syntax allows them, and not
# only at the one its own row reaches. Each is an inline (...)? group of the
# page's rule, which the reader lowers to a rule named after the group; the
# note names the page. Rules whose group stands at one site only are left out.
